areas: Account and listing integrity
Explicit editable-field lists for six listing controllers and veterinarian profiles; stronger generated vet passwords; moderation state and featured flags protected.
OTP authentication

Cryptographic code generation; direct-provider debug output restricted to explicitly enabled development; persistent attempt blocks; existing blocks preserved; row locks prevent code reuse; veterinarian OTPs hashed with cooldown and attempt limits.
Public data and privacy

Published-only blog/scheme feeds; removed listings hidden; moderation notes and internal media keys removed from public pet responses; nearby-user phone exposure removed; sensitive veterinarian documents stored separately and served through admin authentication.
Database consistency

One shared Sequelize configuration; explicit TLS settings and certificate validation; transactional milk/cow updates; unique active appointment slots, daily milk reports, and animal identities; idempotent review helpful votes.
Appointment and date handling

Invalid UUIDs return client errors; terminal status transitions restricted; India business dates used for booking validation and reminders; web booking URLs fetch veterinarian details and survive reload.
Media and AI requests

Original media retained until request succeeds; new uploads cleaned after failure including late parallel completions; failed cow uploads cannot silently succeed; AI image requests restricted to approved HTTPS storage hosts and public DNS addresses with pinned resolution, bounded size, timeout and no redirects.
Notifications and sockets

Failed push sends remain retryable; actual outcomes propagate to callers; blocked recipients are checked before delivery; existing sockets revoked when account access is denied and tokens expire; nearby notification candidates filtered and paginated in PostgreSQL.
Calls, views and API bounds

Recipient/listing ownership checked before recording calls; per-participant history deletion implemented; atomic daily view counting shared across listing routes; pagination/radius bounded; invalid wishlist checks return client errors; production server errors sanitized.
Mobile stability and sessions

Translation-readiness hook order fixed in three screens; conditional hook order corrected in AnimalCard; farmer/vet tokens selected independently; role-specific 401 cleanup; Axios error metadata preserved; account-scoped wishlist cache and species-aware identity; photo upload helper uses supported routes and field names.
Web wishlist and configuration

Server-backed wishlist persistence, seller contacts and per-account cache; async mutation errors propagated to UI; cross-tab session refresh; missing map coordinates distinguished from zero; maps key read from environment; Netlify SPA fallback added.
Release and process lifecycle

Placeholder mobile API URLs removed; preview/production require a real HTTPS endpoint and reject cleartext opt-in; share package corrected and placeholder App Store link removed; SIGTERM/SIGINT close sockets, HTTP, scheduled jobs, timers and database.
deployment: Run npm run runtime:preflight from server against the intended deployment database. This is read-only and reports duplicate IDs plus legacy public document owners. The audit ran it only against isolated local data.

Reconcile any reported duplicate active appointments, daily milk reports or animal identities before running npm run db:migrate. The new migration fails transactionally on duplicates rather than deleting or guessing which business record to keep. Apply migrations before starting the new server.

Configure AWS_S3_PRIVATE_BUCKET as a separate bucket with all S3 public-access blocking enabled and no public bucket policy; grant the backend read/write permissions. New identity-document uploads intentionally fail if separate private storage is missing.

Move existing license, degree and Aadhaar objects out of public storage, update their document and *_public_id columns to private:<bucket>:<key>, verify admin downloads, and remove old public objects and cached CDN copies. The preflight lists affected veterinarian IDs; live object migration was not authorized or performed.

Set the actual HTTPS API URL in preview/production EAS environments and leave EXPO_PUBLIC_ALLOW_CLEARTEXT false. Configure DB_SSL and the trusted CA as needed. Review existing RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS overrides against the new 1000-per-15-minute default.

Set VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY with appropriate origin/API restrictions and rotate or restrict the formerly embedded key. Set EXPO_PUBLIC_IOS_STORE_URL only when the actual App Store URL is available. Real .env files were not modified.
limits: No configured remote database or live SMS, email, push, AI, geocoding or object-storage service was contacted by the application tests. External delivery and provider behavior were simulated locally where needed.

Android and iOS JavaScript/Hermes bundles were exported successfully. Physical-device camera, GPS, permissions, push delivery, native compilation/signing and App Store installation were not tested; no emulator or device was available.
The HTTP route sweep includes four postal-code 500 responses because external geocoding was blocked. These are recorded as provider coverage limitations, not counted as successful provider tests.

The initial public pet-detail check failed before a follow-up fix. Its passing replacement is explicitly recorded in extended-results.json. The booking deep-link problem found by browser follow-up was fixed and retested.
This report covers the inspected code and reproduced cases. Passing tests do not prove that no undiscovered defects remain. No deployment or live-data migration was performed.
